fix(entropy): Only mark callbacks as failed if enough gas was provided, regardless of revert code (#3106)

Summary
This PR removes the check that allows us to mark callbacks as failed (even if enough gas wasn't provided) if they revert with a non-empty return code.

Rationale
When we wrote this initally, we thought that all out-of-gas reverts from calling contracts would bubble up and be caught by the ret.length == 0 condition. However, we have found that some contracts catch out-of-gas reverts and then revert with a different error code. This means we can end up calling these callbacks without enough gas.

Simple fix here is to require enough gas to be provided regardless of the revert code.

fix(insights): fix coming soon list

This is a very obscure, very tricky issue.  I'll try to explain the problem and
fix:

We use the React Compiler on IH, the component library, and a few other places.

There's a limitation where the react compiler only works properly for client
components.  It makes sense given the purpose of the compiler is to add caching
and caching only matters client-side; in general nextjs will handle separating
client from server components and only applying the react compiler to client
components, however it cannot do so in the component library, where the code is
transpiled separately outside of nextjs.

Working with the React Compiler in such an environment is a bit obscure, see the
React ticket [here](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/31702) which
describes the exact issues we've run into in the past.

At the time I first encountered this limitation, it seemed like the best
solution was to mark every component exported by the component library as
`"use client"`.  This works, however it seems to cause errors only in production
mode when passing `ReactNode` props to components exported by the component
library, if the props themselves are not also client components.

This was the case with `<PriceFeedIcon>` being passed in to `<SymbolPairTag>`,
and it was causing the Coming Soon list to throw an exception when rendering.

Marking `<PriceFeedIcon>` as a client component -- while unnecessary
conceptually -- does fix this issue.

In my opinion, this commit is a stopgap solution.  We need to revisit how we use
React Compiler so these kinds of obscure interactions don't happen.  Either we
need a better way of applying the react compiler to the component library, or
perhaps we should just not use react compiler at all if we don't believe it's
stable enough to avoid these kinds of bizarre problems.

fix(insights): use web3.js Connection instead of PythConnection

Upon investigation, it seems the `PythConnection` from `@pythnetwork/client` is
extremely inefficient for a few reasons:

1. `PythConnection` requires loading _all_ account info when creating the
connection class, so that it can build a mapping from price account to program
account.  However IH never used this mapping in practice, so all of that was
wasted work.  This caused major issues for page load performance as loading all
account info from pythnet was a ton of parsing which locked up the browser for
multiple seconds.

2. `PythConnection` did not expose a mechanism to remove unused subscriptions

In doing this I also removed all the live prices contexts since none of that is
needed any more, as well as the call to initialize prices with the last
available price as that too looks unnecessary and redundant.

This change should _drastically_ improve performance in IH, especially during
page load.

feat(developer-hub): add multi-feed search functionality to Lazer price feed IDs

Users can now search for multiple feeds simultaneously by entering
comma or space-separated search terms. For example:
- 'BTC ETH' shows feeds matching either BTC or ETH
- 'BTC, ETH, SOL' shows feeds matching any of the three terms

The search uses OR logic - a feed is shown if it matches ANY of the
search terms.

Co-Authored-By: aditya@dourolabs.xyz <aditya@dourolabs.xyz>

fix(developer-hub): use exact/substring matching for multi-term search

The previous implementation used matchSorter for multi-term search which
caused fuzzy matching to dominate results with the most common term.

For multi-term search (comma/space separated), now uses:
- Exact ID match for numeric terms (e.g., '925' matches pyth_lazer_id 925)
- Case-insensitive substring match for text terms on symbol, name, description

Single-term search still uses matchSorter for fuzzy ranking.

Co-Authored-By: aditya@dourolabs.xyz <aditya@dourolabs.xyz>

fix(developer-hub): prioritize exact ID matches in multi-term search

- Exact ID matches now appear first in search results
- Other matches are sorted by ID for consistent ordering
- Fixes issue where ID 925 was buried in results when searching 'sol, btc, 925'

fix: add remark-math plugin to get-llm-text processor for LaTeX support

The get-llm-text.ts file was missing the remark-math plugin in its
processor chain, causing MDX parsing errors when processing pages
with LaTeX math expressions. The LaTeX content (e.g., \sum containing
\u) was being interpreted as JavaScript Unicode escape sequences.

This fix adds remark-math before remark-mdx in the processor chain,
matching the configuration in source.config.ts, to properly handle
LaTeX math blocks before MDX parsing.

fix(mcp): await httpServer.close() before exiting in shutdown handler

httpServer.close() is async and only completes once active connections
drain. Previously we called close() without awaiting, so in-flight
requests could be cut off during SIGTERM-based rollouts. Now we await
the close callback to ensure graceful connection draining before
flushing logs and exiting.

  /__other__) to prevent unbounded Prometheus cardinality from scanner

  Large) to prevent memory exhaustion from oversized request bodies

During live Claude + Pyth Pro MCP sessions, Claude miscalculated Unix
timestamps (e.g. Jan 1 2025 instead of 2026) and the server's error
responses gave no signal to self-correct. This change makes timestamp
errors self-correcting by:

   and valid data range bounds to get_historical_price and
   get_candlestick_data empty/error responses.

   responses across all tools, giving Claude an anchor for time math.

3. Adding concrete timestamp reference examples to tool descriptions
   for get_historical_price and get_candlestick_data.

4. Adding a new convert_date_to_timestamp helper tool so Claude can
   offload date-to-Unix conversion instead of doing manual math.

5. Wrapping get_historical_price and get_latest_price responses in
   { prices: [...] } (breaking change from bare arrays) to support

fix(dev-hub): make light/dark theme override Lightning CSS prefers-color-scheme polyfill

After #3662 removed the browserslist override, Next.js's wider default
targets cause Lightning CSS to polyfill `light-dark()` using
`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` toggling `--lightningcss-light` /
`--lightningcss-dark` on `:root`. The polyfill ignores the next-themes
`.light` / `.dark` class on `<html>`, so users with OS in dark mode who
toggle the site to light see dark-mode color values on a light
background (and vice-versa) — every `theme.color(...)` call in the
shared theme.scss resolves to the wrong side of `light-dark()`.

Override the polyfill vars on `.light` / `.dark` so the class drives the
toggle, matching the pattern already used for fumadocs vars in this
file. Anchor to `:root.light` / `:root.dark` (specificity 0,2,0) because
Lightning CSS emits the polyfill `:root` rule (0,1,0) per CSS chunk and
some chunks load after global.css — without the `:root.` qualifier the
class-only selector loses the source-order tiebreak.

Verified by toggling class against simulated `prefers-color-scheme:
dark` on the local dev server: text and background colors now resolve
correctly in all four (class, OS) combinations on the homepage and
API reference pages.

fix(dev-hub): use base64url for mermaid.ink URLs

Standard base64 can emit `/` and `+` which are unsafe in URL paths.
A `/` would split the mermaid.ink path (e.g. /svg/abc/def) and cause
a 404. The current TON diagrams happen not to hit it, but any future
diagram whose source contains `?` (or other characters that base64
maps to `/`) would silently break.

base64url (RFC 4648 §5) replaces `+` -> `-` and `/` -> `_`, so the
encoded string is safe to drop directly into a URL path. Verified
mermaid.ink returns 200 for the base64url form.

Spotted by Devin's PR review on #3728.

fix(migration-flow): wrap nuqs consumers in Suspense

Both BranchToggle and BranchSection call useMigrationPath, which is
backed by nuqs useQueryState and ultimately reads useSearchParams
from next/navigation. On Next.js 16, a client component that reads
search params must be wrapped in a Suspense boundary or the entire
host page bails to client-side rendering — which then failed in
production on Vercel with:

  useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary
  page: /price-feeds/core/upgrade
  digest: BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING

Self-wrap each component in Suspense so MDX authors don't have to
think about it:
- BranchToggle: fallback renders an empty radiogroup placeholder.
- BranchSection: fallback renders children at the default-path
  styling (now active, wait muted) so the first paint matches the
  unhydrated state.

ActiveStepHighlighter reads window.location.search directly inside
useEffect rather than useSearchParams, so it doesn't need wrapping.

Verified locally with `pnpm build`: 190/190 static pages generated,
no useSearchParams warnings, no CSR bailout.

ci(message-buffer): fix IDL check and bump actions to Node 24 (#3777)

* ci(message-buffer): fix IDL check and bump actions to Node 24

The "Check IDL changes" CI step was failing because the `fix:format`
turbo task is a no-op — no package defines that script after the
prettier-to-biome migration. Meanwhile, commit d492b530b ran biome on
everything (including IDL files), sorting JSON keys alphabetically via
`useSortedKeys`. CI regenerates IDLs with anchor's default key order,
the no-op format step leaves them unsorted, and `git diff` fails.

Fix: replace the broken `pnpm turbo --filter message_buffer fix:format`
with `npx biome check --write idl/` so the generated IDL files get the
same biome formatting (including sorted keys) as the committed versions.

Also bump deprecated Node-20 GitHub Actions to Node-24 versions:
- actions/checkout@v3 → @v5
- actions/setup-node@v4 → @v5
- pnpm/action-setup@v4 → @v5

feat(price_pusher): add EIP-1559 gas model to EVM pusher (#3779)

* feat(price_pusher): add EIP-1559 gas model to EVM pusher

The EVM pusher priced transactions using the deprecated single `gasPrice`
(legacy) model, sourced from `eth_gasPrice`. Some RPCs mishandle that call in
corner cases, causing transactions to be mispriced or stuck.

Adopt the gas model used by Fortuna, which works well:
- Default to an `eip1559` strategy that computes `maxFeePerGas` from the chain
  base fee (read from the latest block, padded by `--base-fee-multiplier` to
  leave headroom for base fee growth between blocks) plus an estimated priority
  fee (scaled by `--priority-fee-multiplier`). This avoids `eth_gasPrice`.
- Keep a `legacy` strategy (`--gas-pricing-strategy legacy`) for chains that do
  not support EIP-1559 transactions, preserving the previous `--gas-price` and
  custom gas station behaviour.

The fee escalation logic for stuck transactions (override multiplier + cap) is
generalized to work with both strategies.

Adds unit tests for the new gas-price module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(price_pusher): escalate eip1559 priority fee per-component on override

Address review feedback: when replacing a stuck eip1559 transaction, nodes
(e.g. Geth) require both maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas to increase. The
previous min/max selection compared whole gas prices by maxFeePerGas only, so a
freshly-fetched price with a higher maxFeePerGas but lower tip could be chosen,
leaving the replacement underpriced.

Replace the whole-struct min/max with escalateGasPrice, which raises each fee
component independently: it caps total spend via maxFeePerGas and raises the tip
enough to outbid the stuck tx, bounding the tip only by the capped maxFeePerGas
(not by the fresh tip scaled by the cap, which would stall escalation when the
market tip drops).

Also bump to 11.0.0: defaulting to the eip1559 strategy is a breaking change for
non-EIP-1559 chains that upgrade without passing `--gas-pricing-strategy legacy`.

fix(price_pusher): detect "replacement transaction underpriced" across RPC error classes (#3807)

The EVM pusher has a dedicated handler that quietly skips (and escalates on
the next push) when a same-nonce replacement is rejected as underpriced. It
gated on `e instanceof InternalRpcError` && details.includes(...), which
matches the standard Geth encoding (-32000).

Some RPCs encode the same rejection differently: Soneium/Alchemy returns it as
an InvalidInputRpcError (-32602, "Missing or invalid parameters") with the real
reason demoted to the details string. The class check missed it, so the error
fell through to the generic ContractFunctionExecutionError branch and produced
a noisy multi-page warning instead of the intended one-line skip.

Match on the error text across the whole cause chain instead of a specific
viem error class, so detection is robust across providers. Drop the now-unused
InternalRpcError import.

fix(developer-hub): persist changelog baseline via Actions cache, not git

The 3 MB rolling baseline (`data/latest-snapshot.json`) was being
overwritten and committed daily by the workflow, growing git
history despite delta compression. Per REVIEW.md's "No accidental
file commits" rule, generated files should not live in the repo.

Switch to GitHub Actions cache:

  - actions/cache/restore reads the previous baseline at the start
    of each run (key: changelog-baseline; falls back via
    restore-keys for the latest available entry).
  - actions/cache/save writes today's baseline back under a unique
    per-run key; old entries age out via GitHub's 7-day inactivity
    eviction.
  - Cache miss is graceful — the snapshot script bootstraps a
    fresh baseline when the file is absent.

The daily diff JSONs in data/changelog-diffs/ remain committed
(they're small, reviewable, and serve as the audit log).

fix(developer-hub): retry changelog push on conflict, fail loudly

The daily snapshot workflow's bare `git push` could fail
silently if another commit lands on the default branch between
checkout and push, or if branch protection rejects the push.

Add explicit handling:
  - `set -euo pipefail` so any bash failure is loud
  - Retry up to 3 times: on rejection, fetch + rebase against
    `origin/<branch>` and try again
  - After 3 failed attempts, emit `::error::` and exit non-zero
    so the workflow run shows red

The cron is non-blocking — a missed day still self-heals on the
next run (the next-day diff just spans 2 days against the older
cached baseline), but loud failures surface in the Actions UI
rather than going unnoticed.

fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug (#3809)

* fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug

Replace the body of `pyth::set_governance_data_source::execute` with an
unconditional abort so that Pyth governance data source rotation cannot
fire on Sui. This kills the in-PTB replay attack against Sui Pyth
governance (bug bounty report #79076 / i-bouhkykq) without requiring a V2
contract migration.

The replay works because `WormholeVAAVerificationReceipt` carries only
`payload`, `digest`, and `sequence` — it does not bind to the data
source the VAA was verified against. An attacker who has a stale,
previously-signed governance VAA (e.g. `SetDataSources`, `SetUpdateFee`,
`SetStalePriceThreshold`, `SetFeeRecipient`, `ContractUpgrade`) can, in
one PTB, verify both the stale VAA and a fresh `SetGovernanceDataSource`
VAA against the current source, then execute the rotation receipt first.
Rotating the source also overwrites `last_executed_governance_sequence`
with the payload-controlled `initial_sequence`, so the stale receipt
slips past the post-rotation monotonicity check and replays against the
new source.

A proper fix has to bind the data source to the receipt and re-check it
at execute time, which under Sui's `compatible` upgrade policy can only
land as an additive V2 receipt + V2 function variants (changing existing
struct layout or function signatures is rejected by the package upgrade
verifier). Until that V2 upgrade ships, this stopgap closes the
rotation vector and makes the Sui Pyth governance emitter effectively
immutable. The governance source on Sui has been stable since
deployment, so disabling rotation temporarily is an acceptable cost.

Notes:
- Function signature is preserved (parameters underscored to silence
  unused-parameter warnings); this is a body-only change so the package
  upgrade verifier still accepts it under `compatible`.
- The dispatcher in `governance.move` is unchanged and still routes the
  `SetGovernanceDataSource` action to `execute`; the abort happens in
  the callee.
- Removed now-unused imports and the `GovernanceDataSource` /
  `from_byte_vec` helpers (private removals are allowed under
  `compatible`).
- Added an inline regression test that verifies a `SetGovernanceDataSource`
  governance VAA and asserts `execute_governance_instruction` aborts
  with `E_GOVERNANCE_DATA_SOURCE_ROTATION_DISABLED`. The test VAA is
  signed by the well-known Wormhole devnet guardian; the corresponding
  guardian address is wired into `setup_test`.

Local `sui move build` / `sui move test` could not be run in this
sandbox — the project pins Sui rev `041c5f2b` (compiler 1.27.2), which
requires libclang to build from source; the matching pre-built binary
is not published. CI will exercise the gate.

fix(hip-3-pusher): disable loguru diagnose to stop private-key leak in tracebacks (p-kxltpqru)

## Summary

`loguru.logger.add(...)` defaults to `backtrace=True, diagnose=True`. With `diagnose=True`, loguru annotates every traceback frame with the values of all locals in that frame. `Publisher.__init__` (`apps/hip-3-pusher/src/pusher/publisher.py:91-92`) reads the operator's secp256k1 signing key into a local (`oracle_pusher_key`), so any exception escaping while that key is in scope — bad key file, KMS misconfig, `eth_account` validation on a truncated key, any startup error reaching `main.py`'s top-level `logger.exception` — renders the raw hex private key into stderr and every downstream log sink (Loki / CloudWatch / journald).

## Change

`apps/hip-3-pusher/src/pusher/main.py` — `init_logging()` now passes `backtrace=False` and `diagnose=False` by default. Developers can opt back into annotated tracebacks with `LOG_DIAGNOSE=1`; production defaults to off. This is the loguru-documented production hardening.

## Scope

Narrow, per the issue's tactical-fix instruction: only the `logger.add` call named in the finding's root cause is touched. No newtypes / SecretStr wrapping / sibling call-site refactors. Note the same class of leak would recur anywhere a future `logger.add` re-enables `diagnose` while a secret is in a live frame; the defense-in-depth `SecretStr` wrapping is tracked separately and intentionally out of scope here.

## Verification

All four CI-gate commands pass from `apps/hip-3-pusher/`:
- `uv run ruff format src/ tests/` — 28 files unchanged
- `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` — All checks passed
- `uv run mypy src/` — Success, no issues (13 files)
- `uv run pytest tests/` — 19 passed

Behavioral repro confirming the leak is closed: triggered an exception with a secret hex string in a local and logged via the patched `init_logging()`. With `LOG_DIAGNOSE` unset the traceback is clean (no `= '0x...'` frame annotations); with `LOG_DIAGNOSE=1` the annotations return, confirming the dev opt-in still works.

## Suggested reviewers

- `@merolish` (Mike Rolish) — primary committer of `hip-3-pusher/main.py` and CODEOWNER for the sibling `apps/pyth-lazer-agent`
- `@tejasbadadare` (Tejas Badadare) — recent committer to this app

## Changes

- **`target_chains/sui/contracts/Move.toml`** — migrated to the Move 2024 package system (package management v2):

  - Renamed the package `Pyth` → `pyth` so its own named address (`pyth::…`, used throughout sources) resolves under the new scheme, which binds the package name as the root named address. The Move manifest name is metadata only — module IDs and on-chain identity are unaffected.
  - Kept `edition = "legacy"` so **no Move source changes are required**; `package_utils`/`consumed_vaas` and all other wormhole module usages compile unchanged against the new wormhole layout.
  - Regenerated `Move.lock` (v4, mainnet + testnet environments).
- **`lazer/contracts/sui/Move.toml`** — dropped the `pyth-network/wormhole` fork (per its existing TODO), pointing at upstream `wormhole-foundation/wormhole` `c5a2eabe`. - **`.github/workflows/ci-sui-contract.yml`** — install a prebuilt Sui CLI binary (mainnet v1.72.2, mirroring `ci-lazer-sui-contract.yml`) instead of `cargo install`-ing the old pinned rev `041c5f2b`, whose Move git-fetcher bug caused the `Name of dependency 'Wormhole' does not match … 'wormhole'` failures.

- `lazer/contracts/sui`: `sui move build` clean; `sui move test` → 47/47 pass.

The per-network **deployment templates** (`Move.mainnet.toml`, `Move.testnet.toml`, `Move.pro_compatible.sui_*.toml`, and the iota/movement variants) are manual deploy-time configs (operators copy one into `Move.toml` by hand per the README) — they are not exercised by CI. fix(price_pusher): use native gRPC transport for the Sui driver (#3878)

* fix(price_pusher): use native gRPC transport for the Sui driver

The Sui gRPC driver constructed `SuiGrpcClient({ baseUrl, network })`,
which defaults to a grpc-web transport over Node's HTTP/1.1 `fetch`.
Third-party Sui gRPC providers (QuikNode `:9000`, Ankr / BlockVision
`:443`) serve native gRPC over HTTP/2 and reject grpc-web content types,
so every call failed with `fetch failed` / "other side closed". The
default-transport path also silently drops the `meta` option, so no auth
header ever reached the wire; the canary's URL-path token was ignored.

Build an explicit `@protobuf-ts/grpc-transport` (native gRPC over
`@grpc/grpc-js`) instead, and plumb an auth header through its metadata
via a new repeatable `--grpc-metadata key=value` flag (`x-token=...` for
QuikNode/Ankr, `x-api-key=...` for BlockVision). The gRPC endpoint is now
a bare `host:port`; `http://` selects an insecure channel for local
devnet, otherwise TLS. The JSON-RPC path is unchanged.

Verified end-to-end against Sui mainnet over QuikNode gRPC: reads,
balance, gas-pool split, and a real price-update transaction all land;
the JSON-RPC path still works with no regression.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(price_pusher): await tx finality between Sui gas-pool transactions

The gas-pool init chains transactions that each spend the object the
previous one produced (merge chunk i -> chunk i+1, and merge -> split).
Native-gRPC endpoints are load-balanced across fullnodes at slightly
different checkpoints, so the follow-up transaction can be simulated
against a backend that has not yet applied the prior one and fail with
"provided version doesn't match", aborting pusher startup. The legacy
JSON-RPC path got read-your-writes for free via WaitForLocalExecution.
The original single-coin verification never hit this because the merge
is skipped when only one gas coin exists.

Wait for each merge to be observable (the SDK's built-in
core.waitForTransaction) before the next transaction spends its output.
Bump 11.2.1 -> 11.2.2.

fix(price_pusher): bound + single-flight the EVM receipt tracker (stop the getTransactionByHash leak)

The EVM pusher tracked each submitted tx with a fire-and-forget
`void waitForTransactionReceipt(hash)`. On the pinned viem (2.24.3) that call's
timeout rejects WITHOUT tearing down its internal eth_getTransactionByHash /
block-number poll, so a tx that never becomes findable leaves a detached poller
running for the pod's whole lifetime -- one accumulates per push. Measured in
prod: ~1,157 upstream eth_getTransactionByHash/s on Soneium (green), ~197M/day
fleet-wide (Soneium, Eth, Monad, HyperEVM, ...).

Replace it with a bounded, single-flight, cancellable getTransactionReceipt poll:
- caps concurrent waiters at one (each push aborts the prior tracker),
- stops at a deadline (default 60s) so an un-landing tx cannot poll forever,
- issues ZERO eth_getTransactionByHash,
- still logs "Price update successful" {hash} on landing -- even when the tracker
  was superseded (a confirmed receipt is never stale), so the Grafana Tx-Hash
  panel does not miss hashes.

Receipt tracking is observational only: the re-send / nonce / gas decision is
driven by a fresh getTransactionCount each cycle, not the receipt, so nothing on
the hot path changes. Adds dispose() to stop the tracker for graceful shutdown.

Complements deployments#5120 (eRPC hedge-off for eth_getTransactionByHash, which
removes the ~3.15x amplification); this fix removes the leak at the source and
covers every chain regardless of RPC routing. The two are independent.

Tested with a 6-scenario simulation driving the real EvmPricePusher against an
instrumented mock chain.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(price_pusher): keep same-nonce escalation txs watched (address Codex review)

On a same-nonce gas escalation the original and the repriced tx compete for the
nonce, and a miner may include the OLD tx over the replacement. The previous
single-flight design aborted the original's tracker when the replacement was
sent, so if the original landed shortly after, its "Price update successful"
{hash} log was dropped and the Grafana Tx-Hash panel missed a tx that landed.

Track receipts per-nonce instead: same-nonce escalations ADD a tracker (both
competing hashes stay watched, whichever lands is logged), and a nonce ADVANCE
aborts the resolved nonce's stragglers (each does one final lookup on abort, so
the hash that landed is still logged). Still bounded: at most one nonce tracked
at a time and every tracker self-terminates at the deadline. dispose() now stops
all trackers.

Adds two regression tests (old-tx-wins-the-race is logged; nonce-advance aborts
stragglers but still logs the landed tx).

Add pyth-governance-voter CLI for Pyth DAO voting (Fireblocks + hot + Ledger) (#3888)

* feat(governance): add pyth-governance-voter CLI for Pyth DAO voting

Add a new TypeScript CLI package at governance/pyth_governance_voter for
casting votes on Pyth DAO governance proposals. It replaces the manual
Realms UI flow, which does not work with our Fireblocks-custodied vault.

Each vote is a single Solana transaction with two instructions that must
ride together for the freshly computed voter weight to be valid:

  1. updateVoterWeight(CastVote) on the Pyth staking program, with the
     proposal passed as the remaining account the program reads to pin
     the voter weight to the proposal's voting epoch.
  2. castVote on SPL Governance V2, consuming that voter-weight record.

The CLI supports three signing backends: fireblocks (production, RAW
EDDSA_ED25519 signing with polling), hot (local keypair), and ledger.
A --dry-run mode builds the identical transaction, prints a structured
summary of both decoded instructions, and runs simulateTransaction
without sending anything (and without creating a Fireblocks approval
item). Fireblocks credentials are read from environment variables only.

fix(developer-hub): declare .source as a build output for turbo

developer-hub's build task inherited the root outputs list of lib/**,
dist/** and .next/**. The .source directory, which the fumadocs MDX
plugin generates during next build, was not among them and is gitignored.

websocket credential, with the short-lived JWT mentioned solely as a
browser workaround. Pyth Pro accepts either token as the Bearer value,
and integrators migrating for the History auth cutover have been asking
how to use each.

- Step 1: state the both-credentials rule and add a Pro API key /
  Short-lived JWT tab pair (mint via POST /auth/token, then present the
  JWT in place of the key), keeping the security callout and the
  browser subprotocol note.
- Step 3: note that the SDK token field accepts either credential.

Both paths live-verified against production: REST latest_price and the
websocket stream accept the raw key and a minted JWT via the
Authorization header, and the JWT via the pyth-lazer-auth subprotocol.

feat(price_pusher): pay Sui gas from the SIP-58 address balance (#3929)

Replace the Sui pusher's gas-coin pool with SIP-58 address-balance gas. On
startup all owned Coin<SUI> objects are consolidated into the wallet's own
address balance via 0x2::coin::send_funds; each push then pays gas with an
empty gas payment and sources the per-update fee from the address balance
(tx.coin({useGasCoin:false}) + updatePriceFeedsWithCoins). Address-balance
withdrawals settle through the accumulator with no per-object locking, so
concurrent pushes no longer contend on shared gas coins -- removing the pool,
its split/refresh bookkeeping, and the --num-gas-objects flag.

Bumps @mysten/sui 2.7.0 -> 2.22.1 (address-balance support) across
price_pusher, pyth-sui-js, and contract_manager.
